Federated learning enables collaborative model training across multiple devices, 
yet its security is compromised when data is shared across untrusted environments. 
To address this limitation, we introduce Flatee, a federated learning framework 
that securely trains models across trusted environments, such as secure enclaves, 
and untrusted environments, such as cloud services. Flatee achieves this by 
utilizing homomorphic encryption and secure multi-party computation to safeguard 
sensitive data and computations. Our evaluation demonstrates that Flatee 
efficiently trains models on a large-scale dataset, with a 2.5x speedup over 
existing federated learning approaches. Furthermore, Flatee's performance is 
comparable to centralized training methods, with a 1.2x speedup over the latter. 
Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/IBM/Flatee.

The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence in various sectors has led to a pressing need for its transparency and accountability. This study explores the potential of requirements engineering to enhance the explainability of AI systems, focusing on the user's perspective. We examine the current state of explainability in AI, its relationship with requirements engineering, and the challenges involved in integrating these two fields. Furthermore, we outline a framework for developing explainability requirements, which can be applied to various AI applications. This framework is illustrated through a case study involving a medical diagnosis system. Our research aims to contribute to the development of a user-centric approach for requirements engineering in AI systems. This approach prioritizes the user's needs and expectations, which are critical for the successful deployment of AI systems. By integrating requirements engineering with AI, we can create more transparent and accountable systems that meet the user's requirements. This study is a starting point for further research in this area. We hope that our findings will inspire the development of new methods and tools for requirements engineering in AI systems.
